result:
The lower bound checks out. Every count from 0 to 2024 must appear, so some gnome must see all 2024 others, which requires its angular span to be at most α. For the regular 2025-gon, every vertex has span 180·2023/2025, so α below that value fails, and inf S ≥ 180·2023/2025. The convex-hull argument shows this is the right threshold for the count-2024 requirement.

The upper end is not established. The claim sup S = 180 rests on a hand-waved Hall's-condition argument and an informal complement symmetry, not a proof. I could not rule out an obstruction for α close to 180, though the heuristics I tried (uniform-disk and three-cluster configurations) did not produce one. The final sum 16192/45 is the value that results if S = [180·2023/2025, 180), which is a natural shape for the problem's "inf + sup" phrasing.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
CONFIDENCE: 3
